subject: Pathology
summary: Bleeding disorders are conditions where normal hemostasis fails, leading to excessive or prolonged bleeding. They arise from platelet defects, coagulation factor deficiencies, or vascular abnormalities. Clinicians must identify the underlying cause to guide targeted therapy.

sections.p: Bleeding disorders are characterized by spontaneous or trauma‑induced bleeding that is disproportionate to the injury. Diagnosis requires a clinical history, physical exam, and a focused laboratory workup to locate the defect.

whenToSeekHelp: Uncontrolled bleeding, especially intracranial or intra‑abdominal; severe anemia with active bleeding; sudden swelling of a joint; signs of DIC such as petechiae and low fibrinogen

faq.q: What is the most common inherited bleeding disorder?
faq.a: Von Willebrand disease, caused by deficient or defective vWF leading to impaired platelet adhesion and low factor VIII.

faq.q: How do I differentiate hemophilia from von Willebrand disease?
faq.a: Hemophilia shows isolated prolonged aPTT with normal vWF; von Willebrand disease shows prolonged bleeding time, prolonged aPTT, and low vWF antigen/activity.
